theme: GRD: consistency of type and grade across eras 1-9
checked: All 577 links tabulated by type x grade x source shape x citation_specificity x verification_state. Read every quote of the 22 thin_with_verified_primary links, all 67 'gave rise to', all 90 'continued as', all 29 'broke with', all 51 Documented 'in contact with', all WA influenced/argued against/in contact with, 38 Documented links with short quotes, and all 65 secondary-only links. Compared relationship kinds across eras: council condemnation, period-split succession, mission sending, order reform branches, mother-church appointment of bishops, and lone nineteenth-century secondary. Grepped 209 secondary work strings for repo citation. Script-checked citation_specificity and verification_state against the sources, and re-verified 40+ restored secondary quotes verbatim against cic/texts.

findings.finding: Six links rest only on a secondary work, yet carry citation_specificity A, and four carry verified-direct, while none of their sources has a file, lines or quote. They claim an exact line locus the record does not hold, so the claim cannot be re-checked. The era-5 drafts (Draft_GroupA/C/E and Drafting_Record) gave each secondary a vendored file, lines and a verbatim quote. Revision_Round1/Round2 rewrote the sources with only 'kind' and 'work', and the census took that copy. Eras 4, 7, 8 and 9 keep the same kind of vendored secondary with file, lines and quote (e.g. russian-church-nikon-to-holy-synod--the-old-believers--3, russian-church-synodal-century--russian-evangelicals-stundists, georgian-revival-tao-klarjeti--the-georgian-golden-age), and their A grades are backed by them. The visible symptom is two or three identical secondary entries on one link.
findings.evidence: Build/Ministry/Operations/Audits/2026-11-07_links-era-5/Revision_Round1.json (athonite...--kievan-rus...: sources [{kind, work}] only, cs A, verified-direct) vs Draft_GroupA.json (same link: file mouravieff...1842.txt lines 1557-1563 and 1599-1603 with quotes). I re-checked every restored quote against its file: all match. E.g. cic/texts/curzon_visits-to-monasteries-in-the-levant_1849.txt 8704-8705 'St. Laura was founded by Nicephorus Phocas, and restored by Neagulus, Waywode of Bessarabia.'; cic/texts/benedict_rule-of-st-benedict-lat-eng_hunter-blair1907.txt 10527-10529 'the early constitu- tions both of the Carthusian and Cistercian Orders explicitly legislate for conversations at regular times.'

findings.doubts: The Drafting Brief's source shape gives secondaries file/lines/quote = null. Eras 4, 7, 8 and 9 did not follow that letter for vendored secondaries, and the validator ignores secondary quotes. If Mark prefers the brief's letter, the fix instead sets these six to citation_specificity C (B where a chapter is named) and verification_state named-not-rechecked. Either way the current A/verified-direct with nothing behind it is wrong. Restoring is the root-cause fix because the era-5 pass did read these lines (its README says so). Restored entries come from the era-5 Drafting_Record or Draft_Group files. Each census secondary was matched by author to a drafted vendored secondary, and the matched file, lines, locus, quote and license were copied in. The census 'work' strings are unchanged. Whoever applies this should confirm each work string still names the matched passage, because the revision may have reworded a few. The quotes themselves all pass a verbatim check.

findings.finding: The same era-5 revision stripped file, lines and quote from the vendored secondaries of these links too. Each also has a primary at a line locus, so grade, citation_specificity and verification_state stay valid. But the secondary loci the drafters checked are lost, unlike the same works in other eras (Mouravieff, Brosset, McCann, Zimmerman, Rački carry lines in eras 4, 7, 8, 9). Several links now show duplicate identical secondary entries.

findings.finding: The same evidence shape gets two different grades. A link resting on one vendored nineteenth- or early-twentieth-century secondary account that states the tie, read at its lines, with no primary, is Dominant Modern Reconstruction in ten links. Those rest on Mouravieff 1838, Brosset 1849, Rački 1869 and Lutzow 1910, in eras 4-5. The same shape is Inferential-Thin in four links: Curzon 1849 (era 4, drafted in era 5), Anjou 1850 (era 4), Conybeare 1921 (era 6) and Rees 1818 (era 7). Era 5's review (R1-08) moved two links to DMR to match Mouravieff and Brosset, but Curzon in the same era-5 draft set stayed Thin. Several DMR notes say 'This rests on that one modern summary', which is the language of a thin grade. A lone 1838 church history is not plainly a 'dominant modern reconstruction' either.
findings.evidence: anjou...1859.txt 420-423 'The country was visited by teachers, at first from France, afterward chiefly from England'; racovian-catechism...rees1818.txt 3314-3320 'became amalgamated with the Remonstrants and the Mennonites'; conybeare_russian-dissenters_1921.txt 2244-2247 'Joseph Sanin, prior and founder of the Volokolam monastery and his disciples Daniel and Macarius'; curzon 8704-8705 (above). Each states its tie as plainly as Mouravieff 1557-1603 or Brosset 2965-2967. Era-5 Opus_Review_Round1.json R1-08 sets the DMR precedent.
findings.doubts: The grade definitions do not say what a lone pre-modern secondary earns, so this needs one ruling, not case-by-case edits. Option A (recommended): Inferential-Thin for any link whose only support is one pre-1930 secondary account. That is the safer direction, never an upgrade, and the notes already say it rests on one account. It moves 10 links down. Option B: DMR for all, which moves 4 up and rewrites their 'thin' sentences. Option C: DMR only where the repo also cites a modern study for the same reading. Lutzow 1910 on the Moravian mission is borderline, because the event is famous but its own texts are not vendored.

findings.finding: verification_state is used two ways across eras. The Drafting Brief defines verified-direct as 'read the quoted lines ... and they show the claimed relationship'. Yet 22 Inferential-Thin links carry verified-direct, and their own notes say the quotes do not show the relationship. Fifty Widely Accepted links do the same. Most eras read it as 'the quoted lines were read and match'. Like cases elsewhere are marked otherwise. Thin links with read primary quotes are 'unverified' in eras 2 and 9 (desert-monasticism--iconophile..., alaskan-mission--american-orthodoxy...). Twenty-one WA links are 'named-not-rechecked' despite read primary quotes. Vendored secondaries read at lines are 'named-not-rechecked' in era 8 but 'verified-direct' in eras 4, 5 and 9. So the field does not tell a reader the same thing from era to era.
findings.evidence: Drafting_Brief.md 'Per-link fields'. Counts by script over cic-website/data/world-census.json: Thin by era and state (era 2: 5 verified-direct, 2 unverified, 1 named-not-rechecked; era 9: 1 / 2 / 1); WA 50 verified-direct, 21 named-not-rechecked.
findings.doubts: This is a vocabulary ruling, not a per-link fix. Option A: keep the brief's meaning, so Thin, Contested and most WA links move off verified-direct, and Documented keeps it. Option B: redefine verified-direct as 'quoted lines read and matched', and set the outliers to it. The validator only ties verified-direct to Documented, so either option passes.

checked_and_fine: thin_with_verified_primary (22 links): read every quote. Each Thin grade is honest: the quotes show events, places or a name, not the claimed tie, and each note says so. No upgrade is warranted. Only the verification_state wording is at issue (GRD-06).

Cursus Scottorum tract: Thin for desert/Gallic monasticism to Irish (era 2) vs Documented for Irish to Merovingian (era 3). Consistent, because the era-3 link rests on Jonas of Bobbio (Columbanus founded Luxeuil, houses 'under Columban's rule'), with the tract only supporting it.

Same-office succession across a period split: Documented in eras 3-9 where a list or a person spans the split (Bar Hebraeus, Abu Salih, patriarch lists, Pius VII). The two Armenian WA links (before-Bagratids to Bagratid; after-Avarayr) are held down by the drafter because the table entry needs its year header to show the span. That is defensible, not an outlier.

palestinian-church-pre-constantinian--jerusalem (continued as, Thin) vs latin-papal-church-gregorian--avignon (Documented): the papal quotes name the Roman see on both sides. The Jerusalem quotes do not name Macarius's see; I checked the letter at npnf201 lines 64955-64975. The difference is in the evidence.

Mission sending ('gave rise to'): Documented in eras 3, 4, 7 and 9 where a dated text names the missionaries and their arrival or converts. the-baptists--the-missionary-movement-s-native-churches-seramp is Thin because Rippon 1793 shows the sending but not the arrival. No vendored text on Serampore was found (grep), so it is not an outlier.

Reform branches of orders: 'gave rise to' where the parent is in the same window (franciscan-order-era-6 to Observants), 'influenced' where the parent's window ended centuries before (the-carmelites, ending 1300, to the Teresian reform of 1562; the-franciscan-movement to Observants). The rule is applied consistently.

Council or authority condemning a group: 'argued against' (35) when one side's act is shown, 'broke with' (10) when both sides recorded the rupture. One-sided 'broke with' (1054, Schwenckfeld, Welsh Methodists) fits the brief's 'ideally from both sides'. The era-5 note on 1054 says plainly that only the Latin record is quoted.

Secondary works on WA/DMR/Contested links: 209 work strings checked by surname and title-word grep outside the census and link audits. 202 matched automatically; the other 7 (three Cambridge History chapters, Biller, Tarchnischvili, Sempad/Dulaurier, Sinclair via Percival) are cited in Build/ (river-prototype, dossiers, download-queue seed) or inside a vendored text. None is uncited.

Primary vs secondary role of 19th-century histories (Mouravieff, Herberstein, Ormanian, Brosset's editions): primary only where the writer is near-contemporary to the events (Mouravieff's Notes on the 1830s, Herberstein on 1517 Moscow, Ormanian on his own church c.1900), secondary for earlier centuries. The rule is consistent. Embedded documents (Zakaria of Kanaker, Samuel of Ani in Brosset; bulls in Harasiewicz) are rightly primary.

hieronymian-ascetic-literary--homoian-arian-christianity (Documented): the quote lacks the names Valens and Ursacius, but they stand in the same sentence at npnf206 32403-32409 (split by an endnote). The tie is shown, so this is not a grade issue.

Documented links with under-160-character quotes (38 checked): each quote names the other side or shows the act (a text naming Bardaisan, Marcion, Origen, Tatian or Justin; an anathema of Mansur; Symeon's work printed in the Philokalia). None shows only an event.

Shape outliers from feature_by_grade.json (prim2_sec0_A Thin x8, prim1_sec0_A Thin x3, prim2_sec1_A Thin x6) are the Thin links reviewed above. The quotes do not show the relationship, so shape alone did not decide the grade, rightly.
